- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–7 days.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising prices) but sentiment is neutral or negative, suppress momentum; cap forecast increase to 1–2% per day.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending up, model often fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in early periods (e.g., 1–3 days after a spike); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price peaks (last 5–7 days); add 1–3% upward bias if sentiment is positive and price is trending up.
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or slightly down, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
